Fixed the regression in `Statement.get_type()` in sqlparse/sql.py. The condition had been inverted from `token.ttype != T.Keyword.CTE` back to `token.ttype == T.Keyword.CTE`, which is the correct logic for handling the WITH...CTE case (previously it was skipping the CTE-specific traversal that finds the actual DML keyword, causing it to fall through to 'UNKNOWN'). I also added `skip_cm=True` to the `token_next` calls inside that branch so that comments between CTE clauses (issue632) don't interfere with finding the next Identifier/IdentifierList or DML keyword.

Verified with `check` (0 failing, 2 passing) and manual testing of both the basic CTE case and CTE-with-comment case, both returning 'SELECT' as expected.
